commit.message:
BUG: return nan from kempton_taylor_q for a single-taxon sample (#2619)

* BUG: return nan from kempton_taylor_q for a single-taxon sample

* BUG: calculate Kempton-Taylor quantiles with linear interpolation

Use the interquantile fraction of observed taxa for the numerator and
validate ordered quantile probabilities. Return nan for a single observed
taxon and cover narrow ranges, endpoints and tied abundances. Preserve
Boolean count inputs when calculating quantiles.

* DOC: avoid overlapping upstream changelog additions

Place the singleton fix first in Bug Fixes and the quantile change after
Miscellaneous. Keep both entries within the current development release.

* BUG: preserve the Kempton-Taylor calculation when guarding inputs

Restore the inward-rounded indices, numerator and scientific documentation.
Return nan for fewer than two observed taxa and reject invalid probabilities
or reversed or out-of-bounds rounded indices.

* BUG: handle undefined Kempton-Taylor intervals

Co-authored-by: Qiyun Zhu <4396343+qiyunzhu@users.noreply.github.com>

* TST: keep alpha metric tests focused on individual vectors

* DOC: resolve changelog conflict with main

* Refactor ValueError message for quantile validation

Refactor error message formatting and improve readability in quantile validation.

---------

Co-authored-by: Qiyun Zhu <4396343+qiyunzhu@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Qiyun Zhu <qiyunzhu@gmail.com>

@@ -18,19 +18,22 @@
 
 * Fixed `ancombc2` producing NaN results when Gaussian mixture densities underflow to zero during bias estimation ([#2631](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/issues/2631)).
 * Fixed `GrammaredSequence` subclasses with extended alphabets incorrectly inheriting cached character masks from their parent class ([#2620](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2620)).
+* Fixed `kempton_taylor_q` raising `IndexError` on a sample containing a single taxon, which aborted `alpha_diversity` for the whole table. It now returns `nan` if the interquantile range is empty or constant, and accepts `upper_quantile=1`. Quantiles that do not satisfy `0 <= lower_quantile < upper_quantile <= 1` raise `ValueError` ([#2619](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2619)).
 * Fixed `GrammaredSequence` grammar definitions with multi-character symbols so they fail upon class creation rather than later during sequence operations ([#2620](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2620)).
 * Fixed a loophole in `Sequence` construction admitting extended ASCII codes (128-255) if supplied as bytes or a uint8 array. Construction now by default validates ASCII codes (0-127) ([#2614](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2614)).
 * Fixed a loophole in `Sequence` construction referring to an external array while flagging it as read-only, whereas one can still unflag the array and mutate its content. Construction now by default enforces immutability, and an external array is copied rather than referred ([#2614](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2614)).
 * Corrected an inaccurate statement in the documentation of `Protein`, which should have 22 definite characters (including 'O' and 'U') instead of 20 ([#2621](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/pull/2621)).
 * Fixed a broken link to `Sequence.iter_kmers` in the feature highlights on the documentation front page ([#2605](https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio/issues/2605)).
 * Fixed `Sequence` case conversion altering characters that are not letters. `Sequence.lowercase` (used by the `lowercase` option of the FASTA and FASTQ writers) flipped the case bit of every selected character. When a lowercase mask covered non-letter positions, gaps (`-`), dots (`.`) and stop codons (`*`) were turned into control characters (e.g., `\r` and `\n`), and lowercase letters were converted to uppercase. The `lowercase` parameter of `Sequence` treated every character after `Z` as lowercase, rewriting `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `_`, `` ` ``, `{`, `|`, `}` and `~`. Case conversion is now restricted to the letters A-Z and a-z.
 
-
 ### Miscellaneous
 
 * `GrammaredSequence` subclasses may define only `definite_chars`, without defining gap or degenerate characters. When a subclass defines `gap_chars` but not `default_gap_char`, its first sorted gap character is used as the default.
 
 
+### Backward-incompatible changes
+

@@ -239,6 +239,44 @@ def test_kempton_taylor_q(self):
 
         self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([0, 0])))
 
+    def test_kempton_taylor_q_single_taxon(self):
+        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([])))
+        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([5])))
+        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([0, 5, 0])))
+        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([False, True, False])))
+        self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([5], 0, 1)))
+
+    def test_kempton_taylor_q_quantiles(self):
+        counts = np.arange(1, 11)
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(kempton_taylor_q(counts, 0.1, 0.9),
+                               8 / np.log(10 / 2))
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(kempton_taylor_q(counts, 0, 0.9),
+                               9 / np.log(10))
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(kempton_taylor_q(counts, 0, np.nextafter(1., 0.)),
+                               9 / np.log(10))
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(kempton_taylor_q(counts, 0, 1), 9 / np.log(10))
+        self.assertAlmostEqual(kempton_taylor_q([1, 2], 0, 1), 1 / np.log(2))
+
+    def test_kempton_taylor_q_degenerate_intervals(self):
+        with np.errstate(divide="raise", invalid="raise"):
+            self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([1, 2])))
+            self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([5, 5])))
+            self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([5, 5, 5, 5])))
+            self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([True, True, True])))
+            self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([1, 2, 3], 0.5, 0.6)))
+            self.assertTrue(np.isnan(kempton_taylor_q([1, 2, 3], 0.8, 0.9)))
+
+    def test_kempton_taylor_q_invalid_quantiles(self):
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            kempton_taylor_q([], 0.5, 0.5)
+        for lower, upper in [(-0.1, 0.75), (0.25, 1.1),
+                             (0.75, 0.25), (0.5, 0.5),
+                             (np.nan, 0.75), (0.25, np.nan),
+                             (-np.inf, 0.75), (0.25, np.inf)]:
+            with self.subTest(lower=lower, upper=upper):
+                with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Quantiles must satisfy"):
+                    kempton_taylor_q([1, 2, 3], lower, upper)
+
     def test_margalef(self):
